title: Compute complex transmission coefficients for the two polarizations
action: Implement the Marcuvitz complex impedance formulas for an infinitely thin plane grating situated at the boundary between two semi-infinite media of refractive indices 2.2 (support) and 1.0 (air). Compute the complex amplitude transmission coefficients for the two orthogonal linear polarizations (electric field parallel and perpendicular to the grid wires) as functions of the ratios a/λ and d/a.
description: Intermediate computational step that produces the complex transmission coefficients required for the subsequent Δ calculation. No explicit output artifact is required; the step must be executed within the same pipeline that produces the final CSV.

title: Calculate relative phase retardance Δ and write CSV
action: Using the transmission coefficients from step 00, compute the relative phase retardance Δ = arg(T_perp) - arg(T_par) (radians). Evaluate Δ for a logarithmically spaced grid of a/λ from 0.001 to 1.0 (at least 50 distinct points) and for d/a values of 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8. Write the results to delta_vs_a_lambda.csv.
description: CSV file containing the computed relative phase retardance Δ values. Each row corresponds to one (a/λ, d/a) pair.
output_schema: Columns: a_lambda (float, dimensionless ratio of grating period to wavelength), d_a (float, dimensionless ratio of conductor width to grating period), Delta (float, relative phase retardance in radians). No header row is required but recommended. At least 50 rows per d_a value, covering a_lambda in logarithmic steps from 0.001 to 1.0.
